doctrine: Strategic Multi-Alignment & Zero-Problems Regional Stability — Saudi Arabia operates as an independent regional heavyweight and global energy anchor, balancing relations among global powers (USA, China, Russia) while creating regional stability and de-escalation necessary to guarantee the execution of Vision 2030.
strategic_priorities: Safeguard global energy markets and OPEC+ production discipline in strategic coordination with Russia and Gulf producers
Preserve regional stability and protect mega-investments through tactical diplomatic rapprochement with Iran and border stabilization with Yemen

Leverage sovereign balance between the United States (irreplaceable defense guarantor and advanced technology partner) and China (top crude oil customer, critical infrastructure contractor, and AI collaborator)
Condition potential normalization with Israel on irreversible, credible pathways toward an independent Palestinian state
Localize defense industrial production to 50% through Saudi Arabian Military Industries (SAMI) while acquiring advanced multi-tier missile and drone defenses
priority_regions: Middle East & Gulf (Gulf Cooperation Council [GCC], Yemen, Iraq, Jordan, Egypt)
Indo-Pacific & East Asia (China, India, Japan, South Korea — primary destinations for Saudi crude exports and trade partnerships)
North America (United States — defense supply chains, intelligence sharing, investment destination)
Red Sea & Horn of Africa (Sudan, Somalia, Djibouti — securing the Red Sea maritime lifeline against piracy and asymmetric threats)

cooperates_closely_with: United States (core security partner, arms supplier, intelligence collaborator, bilateral nuclear talks)
China (largest trade partner, primary oil purchaser, mediator of Iran deal, technological infrastructure contractor)
Russia (co-leader of the OPEC+ oil production alliance managing global crude supply and price stability)
United Arab Emirates & GCC (shared Gulf security and economic integration, despite friendly economic competition)
Egypt & Jordan (foundational Arab security and geopolitical allies across the Red Sea corridor)
India & South Korea (vital long-term energy off-takers and industrial infrastructure partners)
competes_or_disputes_with: Iran / Axis of Resistance (enduring ideological, sectarian, and regional influence rivalry, despite the 2023 diplomatic detente)
Houthi Movement in Yemen (persistent threat to southern borders and Red Sea maritime commerce)
Regional extremist networks (Muslim Brotherhood ideological challenge to monarchical legitimacy, Al-Qaeda / ISIS remnants)
cooperation_and_competition.notes: Saudi Arabia has transformed its diplomatic posture from an era of ideological containment into a transaction-driven foreign policy. Riyadh uses its immense sovereign capital and oil swing capacity to refuse binary choices between Washington and Beijing, extracting maximum strategic advantages from both.

_meta.data_quality: sourced/analytical synthesis based on Saudi Ministry of Foreign Affairs, speeches of Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, and international diplomatic agreements
